children: The most recent quarter likely marks a trough in Pernod Ricard's revenue progress, with inventory effects and comparison bases offering a boost for the months ahead, Jefferies's Edward Mundy writes in a note to clients. The French spirits group, maker of Martell cognac and Jameson whisky among other labels, reported a 0.9% organic decline in net sales for the July-September quarter, a result that was better than expected. "The fiscal first quarter should mark the trough: Destocking is front-loaded and [comparatives] ease from the second quarter," Mundy notes. "As investor confidence increases on the end of the downgrade cycle, this should drive a re-rating." Jefferies has a buy rating and a 90-euro target on the Paris-listed stock; shares open 1.6% higher at 66.54 euros.(joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)
